detail.abstract: Blockchain-based traceability platforms promised to replace fragmented, tier-by-tier record reconciliation across food supply chains with near-instant end-to-end queries. This paper examines when a shared distributed ledger adds value to food traceability beyond incumbent enterprise systems. The paper first conducts an evidence-graded case analysis of IBM Food Trust's 2021-2023 retrenchment, including the discontinuation of its sister network TradeLens and the platform's subsequent compliance-oriented repositioning. From this record, it derives five applicability conditions, organized by a dual-axis lens of traceability directionality and product physicality: party structure, commercial confidentiality, trustworthiness at the point of data creation, institutional alternatives, and commercial viability. The framework is then applied to Taiwan's 2026 contaminated-oil incident as a structural illustration rather than an empirical test: the implicated upstream manufacturer is jointly owned by its principal downstream buyers, regulators reported inconsistencies between upstream and downstream test results, and the blended nature of the commodity constrains forward tracing. The paper further identifies an attestation paradox: where a ledger depends on a trusted certifier to establish that its records correspond to physical reality, the assurance burden rests on that certifier rather than on the ledger. The analysis suggests that blockchain's value in food traceability is conditional rather than categorical: where data veracity depends on trusted certifiers, where parties are equity-bound, or where demand is compliance-driven, incumbent centralized architectures remain the appropriate baseline.

detail.abstract:
Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models have outgrown the high-bandwidth memory of the accelerators that serve them, and offloading expert weights to host memory has become a standard response. This makes expert cache management an attractive lever: if a smarter policy raised the hit rate, the same model would need less expert traffic per token. Evaluating that hypothesis is a measurement problem, and we find the measurement fragile. 

Using a trace-driven, event-atomic simulator over three MoE models (40, 64 and 128 experts), we isolate three evaluation axes that change conclusions rather than shift numbers. Replay semantics: under a fused-event traffic contract, an inconsistent per-access replay inflates recency-based policies by 27-29% while leaving frequency-based and static policies within 4%, inverting the policy ranking. Workload contamination: probe sets using one instruction template per category produce verbatim-identical generation prefixes; a matchedpair rendering intervention moves the measured early-window effect by 19.4-31.9 percentage points and reverses which workloads appear most cache-friendly. Operating regimes: normalized miss fractions do not transfer across models, so the per-step expert union relative to per-layer capacity must be reported-though permuting only the temporal order of an otherwise identical event stream moves the offline-optimal gap from 44.9% to 30.8%, so it is not sufficient. 

After correcting all three, a stable gap to the offline optimum remains (44.2-45.9% across 13 frozen workload compositions). A forced-admission oracle attributes 84.3-96.6% of it to knowing which resident expert is used furthest in the future. A causal next-use predictor, used as an eviction rule, recovers-11.4% of the gap; at the decision points it selects an optimal victim 3.4% of the time against 2.4% for a random resident block and 20.6-22.1% for LRU and LFRU. Our position is narrow: in our evaluated settings a large offline-optimal gap substantially overstates the gains recovered by representative lightweight causal mechanisms. On publication we will release the simulator, a diversity-controlled probe set, the contamination diagnostics and a reporting checklist, subject to the upstream licences recorded in the artifact matrix.

title: ADAM Earned Authority Kernel A Constitutional Execution Architecture for Governed Human and Machine Agency

detail.title: ADAM Earned Authority Kernel A Constitutional Execution Architecture for Governed Human and Machine Agency
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence changes the fundamental security problem of computing. Traditional software largely executes predetermined logic under permissions assigned to users, applications, services, and machines. Agentic systems are different. They reason about goals, generate plans, synthesize software, discover alternative paths, invoke tools, coordinate other agents, and adapt their actions as circumstances change. As these systems become more capable, the decisive architectural question is no longer merely whether an agent possesses a technical capability. The question is whether the agent has legitimately acquired the authority to exercise that capability in a particular context. The ADAM Earned Authority Kernel, or EAK, is the constitutional execution subsystem of ADAM, the Adaptive Development and Assurance Machine (Reddy, 2026a). It establishes the machine-enforced boundary between what an actor is technically capable of doing and what that actor is presently authorized to do. EAK treats humans and agents as first-class actors, separates competency from authority, binds authority to purpose and consequence, translates abstract authorization into enforceable runtime capabilities, and records the evidence necessary to reconstruct why an action was permitted and what occurred when that authority was exercised. Its governing principle is: Performance is observed. Competency is established from evidence. Authority is earned or delegated. Every exercise of authority remains bounded, revocable, attributable, and reconstructable. Earned authority does not imply that every privilege can be autonomously acquired. Some authority may be earned through demonstrated competency, some may require delegation, some may require explicit human approval, and some may remain constitutionally unavailable to particular classes of actors. EAK therefore combines evidence, competency, policy, delegation, consequence, context, and runtime enforcement rather than reducing authorization to a trust score or role assignment. This architecture extends established security principles rather than replacing them. Least privilege, fail-safe defaults, complete mediation, and separation of privilege have been foundational principles of secure system design for decades (Saltzer & Schroeder, 1975). Capability-oriented computing similarly established the importance of associating authority with explicit references and controlled access to computational objects (Dennis & Van Horn, 1966). More recently, zero-trust architecture has reinforced the principle that trust should not be implicitly granted merely because an actor has entered a particular environment and that resource access should be continuously evaluated and minimized (Rose et al., 2020). EAK applies these principles to a new problem: autonomous actors whose capabilities and behavior can change dynamically. ADAM Earned Authority Kernel Reddy, 451 Labs WebAssembly, WASI, WIT, and Wasmtime provide an especially useful first execution substrate because they allow ADAM to instantiate software within a deliberately restricted environment. WebAssembly defines a safe, portable, low-level code format; the Component Model introduces typed component boundaries; WIT describes the interfaces a component provides and requires; and WASI supplies standardized host-facing interfaces (Bytecode Alliance, 2026a, 2026b, 2026c; WebAssembly Community Group, 2026b; World Wide Web Consortium, 2026). These technologies are not EAK itself. EAK is substrate-independent and may ultimately govern WebAssembly components, isolated processes, containers, microVMs, cloud operations, APIs, databases, robots, model invocations, and other consequential resources through appropriate enforcement adapters. The first reference implementation deliberately used a much smaller footprint. A Rust host, a WebAssembly component, a WIT contract, deterministic policy and competency rules, and a tamper-evident evidence ledger were sufficient to validate the constitutional mechanism end to end before integrating the broader ADAM architecture.

detail.abstract: Between elections, the opinion of the Zambian people has no institutional form. Members of Parliament vote on matters that shape millions of lives, while the views of their constituents remain unmeasured, unrecorded, and therefore unclaimable. This paper advances a claim of value: that continuous, deliberated, and universally accessible measurement of citizen opinion-delivered through technology that reaches every Zambian, from the smartphone user in Lusaka to the feature-phone user in Shang'ombo-is a democratic good of the first order, and its absence a measurable deficiency in representative government. Evaluated against four criteria drawn from democratic theory (legitimacy, inclusiveness, accountability, and deliberative quality), a multi-channel participation platform is shown to strengthen rather than rival representative institutions. Evidence is drawn from working precedents in Taiwan, Brazil, and Spain, and from Zambia's own institutional openings: the Constituency Development Fund Act of 2024, which already mandates community participation; the Access to Information Act of 2023; and survey evidence showing that Zambians overwhelmingly prefer democracy while growing steadily less satisfied with how it is practised. The paper argues that the tools to close this gap now exist, that their marginal cost approaches one cent per citizen voice, and that their value is therefore not speculative but forgone daily.

title: Shannon's Chess Machine at Seventy-five: Evaluation, Search and Generative Bayesian Computation
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business and George Mason University

detail.title: Shannon's Chess Machine at Seventy-five: Evaluation, Search and Generative Bayesian Computation
detail.abstract: Shannon's 1950 paper Programming a Computer for Playing Chess decomposes game playing into three objects: an evaluation function f (P) scoring a position, a stability criterion g(P) saying where that score can be trusted, and a plausibility function h(P, M) saying where to spend search. Shannon specified all three by hand and said plainly that the coefficients ought to be determined by some experimental procedure he could not supply. This paper supplies one. We read the 1950 design through modern eyes, and then apply Generative Bayesian Computation-in which a quantile neural network learns an inverse map θ = H(τ, S(y)) carrying a uniform baseline to the posterior-to Shannon's own problem. Three results follow. Player strengths in a Bradley-Terry model are recovered from tournament results at a cost that amortises across data sets. A Bayesian evaluation function returns a posterior over the value of a position whose spread widens automatically with tactical volatility, so that Shannon's g(P) emerges as estimated uncertainty rather than a hand-set flag. And search allocation becomes a decision problem in which posterior-based rules halve the regret of Shannon's Type A uniform search, while rules using only the value or only the uncertainty fail equally badly. We report the method's failures-mild underdispersion, prior-predictive support, a tree-backup problem we do not solve-alongside its successes.

title: The Price of Permission: Classification Uncertainty in Constrained Capital Markets
affiliations: University of College London, University of College London and University of College London

detail.title: The Price of Permission: Classification Uncertainty in Constrained Capital Markets
detail.abstract: Shariah-compliant equity screening provides a transparent setting in which institutional rules determine who may own a stock. A binary label identifies current eligibility but not whether the feasible investor base is fragmented across standards or close to changing. We define this instability as classification uncertainty and formalize its investor-base consequence through permitted investor mass. In a 1999-2024 CRSP-Compustat panel of 13,188 securities classified under seven researcher-emulated Shariah rulebooks, screening-rule disagreement and proximity to active boundaries rank next-month screen-implied transitions. U.S. Fama-MacBeth diagnostics do not support an unconditional equal-weighted permission premium, and a September 2023 DJIM/S&P methodology change produces no robust matched repricing. The central event evidence uses 25 official Securities Commission Malaysia lists. The 410 inclusions already trading before the preceding review have positive but imprecise matched returns. Applying the pre-event turnover floor yields 295 inclusions with 1.76 percentage points over [0, 10] trading days (p date = 0.008; p wild = 0.017) and 2.25 points over [0, 20] (p date = 0.018; p wild = 0.035). Leaveone-date-out, first-inclusion-only, and mid-review placebo checks are supportive, although a joint 20-day pre-event test rejects. Ownership and demand-pressure diagnostics do not identify a unique marginal buyer or clean causal demand shock. The evidence supports treating classification risk as a portfolio-monitoring state. Official Shariah permission is associated with price effects in a recognized local market among sufficiently tradable securities; formal eligibility alone is insufficient.

title: The As-efficient Competitor: Test, Threshold or Principle after the Court of Justice's Google Android Judgment
affiliations: University of East London, School of Law

detail.title: The As-efficient Competitor: Test, Threshold or Principle after the Court of Justice's Google Android Judgment

declarations.funderStatement: none

detail.abstract: In Google Android, the Court of Justice held that the capability to exclude a competitor as efficient as the dominant undertaking is not an invariably applicable condition for establishing abuse under Article 102 TFEU. • The apparent inconsistency with the preceding case law results from the use of AEC terminology for three distinct inquiries: a price-cost test, the review of an AEC analysis relied on as evidence, and a general requirement that the conduct be capable of excluding an as-efficient competitor. • Google Android directly rejects the third proposition. Price-cost tests and other AEC analyses remain available as conduct-specific evidentiary tools where they correspond to the alleged foreclosure mechanism. • The judgment does not remove the need to distinguish anticompetitive foreclosure from exclusion resulting from competition on the merits, and the assessment must therefore identify the competitive constraint, specify the foreclosure mechanism, and establish the causal contribution of the impugned conduct.

title: Ontologies, Predictive Distributions, and Decisions on the Enterprise Knowledge Graph
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business and George Mason University

detail.title: Ontologies, Predictive Distributions, and Decisions on the Enterprise Knowledge Graph
detail.abstract: Enterprise ontologies, the object and action models now standard in operational data platforms, are usually justified as data integration artifacts. We argue instead that they are the layer which makes statistical decision theory executable, and we quantify the claim. An ontology is formally a heterogeneous attributed graph, and recognising this makes precise a question firms actually face: how far along its links must one traverse before the data stops improving decisions? We construct a synthetic retail replenishment environment with known ground truth, in which supplier reliability and distribution centre congestion, both two link traversals from the decision, govern the dispersion of demand while product and store attributes govern its location. Poisson regression, gradient boosting, and monotone quantile neural networks are fitted at increasing hop depth and scored twice, statistically by pinball loss and calibration, and economically by realised newsvendor profit measured against an oracle. Four results follow. First, replacing a fixed buffer heuristic with the correct critical fractile raises profit from 90.0 to 99.3 percent of oracle, which dominates any change of model class. Second, across ten independently drawn environments the first link traversal is worth 4.27 percentage points of profit while the second is worth 0.04, so returns to ontology breadth diminish early. Third, the second traversal nonetheless improves the predictive distribution reliably, with a paired t statistic of-4.5 on pinball loss, because relational context of this kind carries information about uncertainty rather than about expectation; consequently root mean squared error fails to order decision quality at all. Fourth, that apparent contradiction resolves once the loss is allowed to vary. Since newsvendor cost at fractile α ⋆ is proportional to pinball loss at level α ⋆ , we can sweep the economics without refitting. The second traversal is worthless below α ⋆ ≈ 0.80 and then climbs steeply, cutting regret by sixty percent at α ⋆ = 0.99. The value of deep relational context is thus a property of the loss as much as of the data. We also show that action writeback logs are observational rather than experimental: a naive analysis of expediting decisions recovers the wrong sign.

title: Do we Really know What we Think we know about Investors' Reliance on GAAP and Non-GAAP Earnings?
affiliations: University of Georgia - J.M. Tull School of Accounting, University of Georgia, Brigham Young University - Marriott School of Business, University of Georgia and

detail.title: Do we Really know What we Think we know about Investors' Reliance on GAAP and Non-GAAP Earnings?
detail.abstract: Prior research concludes that investors perceive non-GAAP earnings to be more informative than GAAP earnings. We argue that this interpretation is too broad because, following Regulation G, investors simultaneously observe GAAP earnings, non-GAAP earnings, and the reconciliation between them. Consequently, commonly used empirical models identify investors’ responses to the joint information conveyed by these disclosures, rather than a general preference for one earnings measure viewed in isolation. Because these measures are exact linear combinations of one another, the estimated coefficients from relevant regression models yield specific, limited interpretations. We clarify these interpretations by defining three distinct effects—the “included income effect,” the “excluded income effect,” and the “composition effect”—and demonstrate how alternative regression specifications provide equivalent economic inferences, conditional on the appropriate treatment of outlier observations. We find that both investors and analysts respond to all three effects, with the composition effect providing a broad measure of the decision-usefulness of non-GAAP disclosures. These responses have remained remarkably stable over the past two decades despite substantial growth in non-GAAP reporting, yet vary considerably across firms. Our results refine the interpretation of prior research on investor responses to non-GAAP disclosures and inform future research and ongoing policy discussions regarding non-GAAP reporting.

detail.title:
KITEMEO
Artists Beware: The Kapitani-Master VK Beef and the Underlying Legal Issue of Joint Authorship.

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Kitemeo is an alleged collaborative musical work jointly created by Kapitani and Master VK. This article recognises their respective creative contributions and treats the work as an example through which the legal principles governing joint authorship in Kenya may be examined.

detail.abstract: This article examines the doctrine of joint authorship under Kenyan copyright law, using Kapitani-Master VK's beef as a case study to interrogate the legal and practical challenges arising where multiple contributors participate in the creation of a musical work. It considers the distinction between individual contribution and authorship and evaluates the circumstances in which collaborators may acquire joint copyright ownership. The article further examines the Copyright Act and relevant judicial principles governing joint authorship, with particular attention to the requirement that contributions be sufficiently connected to the creation of the protected work. By applying these principles to contemporary music production, the article highlights the difficulties of determining ownership where songwriting, composition, performance, production and other creative contributions overlap. It argues that Kenya’s existing copyright framework, while recognising joint authorship, leaves significant uncertainty regarding the threshold for establishing joint ownership in collaborative musical works. The article therefore advocates for a more context-sensitive approach that accommodates the realities of modern music production while preserving clear standards for determining authorship and ownership.

title: Leverage Products, Foreign Flows, and the Volatility of their Targets

detail.title: Leverage Products, Foreign Flows, and the Volatility of their Targets
detail.abstract: On 27 May 2026 the Korea Exchange listed the country's first single-stock leverage products-sixteen ±2× exchange-traded funds and two exchange-traded notes, on just two eligible underlyings, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. Using survivorship-free daily prices, the leverage products' own trading records, and daily foreign-investor flows from the Korea Exchange, this paper examines whether the products amplified the volatility of their targets, and whether any such effect can be separated from the contemporaneous artificial-intelligence rally and from a record foreign-selling wave. Realized volatility of both stocks roughly doubled after launch, but a difference-indifferences against global memory-chip peers is statistically insignificant: the surge is largely the rally. Within the post-launch period, leverage-ETF trading is significantly associated with the volatility of SK Hynix-whose products, at roughly 51% of its own daily turnover, loom far larger than Samsung's at 18%-in a clear dose-response pattern, and this association survives controlling for foreign flows. Foreign investors net-sold ₩142 trillion of the two stocks over the sample, yet foreign flow is a weak daily driver of volatility, and the leverage association is not a proxy for it. A lead-lag analysis indicates the leverage relationship is bidirectional, consistent with a feedback loop rather than one-directional amplification. Because the post-launch window is short and daily data cannot resolve causal direction, the evidence is early and associational; the identification of a causal mechanism awaits intraday closing-auction data. The paper provides the first evidence on single-stock leverage products and, methodologically, illustrates separating overlapping drivers of volatility using within-period and lead-lag tests where a naive event study cannot.

title: is Global Inflation Coming Back?

detail.title: is Global Inflation Coming Back?
detail.abstract: Throughout 2021-2024 the world has seen numerous inflationary shocks. The monetary policy across the globe went full cycle from tightening to easing in an attempt to tame price increases. In fact, central banks seem ed to succeed in their actions. Nevertheless, as of early 2025 there are various cautious notions pointing out the possibility of the resurge of inflation. Comparative analysis proves that it is quite likely to happen in the mid term, viz. 2025-2026.

title: Risk-Taking in High-stakes Competition: Evidence from Olympic Indoor Volleyball
affiliations: New Economic School (NES), HSE University and

detail.title: Risk-Taking in High-stakes Competition: Evidence from Olympic Indoor Volleyball
detail.abstract: How do elite athletes adjust risk-taking across score contexts and tournament stages, and how do these patterns differ between men's and women's tournaments? We address these questions using a novel, manually coded rally-level dataset from the 2024 Olympic volleyball tournaments, covering 8,670 rallies from 52 men's and women's matches. We operationalize risk through observable tactical choices-serve type and attack placement-and estimate how these choices respond to score context, set progression, and playoff stakes. We find that risk-taking is systematically gendered and context-dependent: men attempt riskier serves as sets near their end, while women grow more conservative when protecting a set lead. In attacking, both genders turn more cautious late in sets. This asymmetry aligns with prospect theory since serving is a loss-domain decision that invites risk-seeking, while attacking is a gain-domain decision that invites risk aversion. Contrary to expectations of caution under elimination pressure, both genders take more risks in the knockout stage. These findings extend behavioral models of risk to a high-stakes team sport setting, with implications for coaching and performance analysis.

title: The Great Convergence Acceleration — Quantifying How Falling Costs in Connectivity, Compute, Clean Energy, and Genomics Simultaneously Compress Development Timelines

detail.title: The Great Convergence Acceleration — Quantifying How Falling Costs in Connectivity, Compute, Clean Energy, and Genomics Simultaneously Compress Development Timelines
detail.abstract:
The report argues that global development is undergoing a historic tempo shift driven by the simultaneous collapse in four foundational technology costs: connectivity, compute, clean energy, and genomics. Each domain has experienced 96–99.9998% cost declines since 2000, but the core finding is that these curves are multiplicative, not independent. As the document states, “their combined Convergence Index has fallen from 100 (2000) to 0.13 (2023), a 99.87% decline.”

This convergence is compressing development timelines from centuries to decades—and in some cases, to mere years. Connectivity costs fell 99.9%, compute costs 99.998%, solar LCOE 96%, and genome sequencing 99.9998%, enabling late-developing countries to leapfrog legacy infrastructure and adopt frontier technologies directly. As the report notes, “technologies that once required 50–90 years to reach mass adoption now achieve 50% global penetration in under 15 years.”

The report introduces the Convergence Index, a geometric mean of normalized cost curves, showing accelerating decline across three eras: Sequential (2000–2007), Converging (2007–2015), and Compounding (2015–present). Cross‑domain amplification—compute accelerating genomics, clean energy powering compute, connectivity distributing both—creates a flywheel that speeds diffusion and reduces barriers to adoption.

Country case studies (Kenya, India, Rwanda, Bangladesh) illustrate how latecomers increasingly outperform historical development timelines by leveraging mobile-first systems, digital public infrastructure, distributed solar, drone logistics, and portable genomics.

Looking forward, the report projects the Convergence Index falling below 0.01 by 2040, implying foundational technology costs at <1% of year‑2000 levels. This shift challenges traditional development models and suggests a transition from sequential to convergent development, with profound implications for policy, industrial strategy, and global inequality.

title: When One Word Moves Twenty-Five Months: Circuit Splits, Mandatory Minimums, and Federal Sentencing
affiliations: Soka University

detail.title: When One Word Moves Twenty-Five Months: Circuit Splits, Mandatory Minimums, and Federal Sentencing
detail.abstract: Federal appellate courts sometimes assign different meanings to the same statute. We study a circuit split over the word "and" in the First Step Act's expanded drug-sentencing safety valve. The Ninth, Eleventh, and later Fourth Circuits interpreted the provision broadly, while four other circuits adopted a restrictive reading. The Supreme Court imposed the restrictive interpretation nationwide in Pulsifer v. United States. Using defendant-level U.S. Sentencing Commission data for fiscal years 2020-2025, we estimate triple differences between criminalhistory profiles, circuit groups, and sentences imposed before and after each precedent. The primary sample contains cases in which the drug mandatory minimum exceeds the guideline floor reconstructed without the safety-valve reduction and excludes cases with a §924(c) charge. Broad interpretations increased recorded statutory safety-valve relief by 48-69 percentage points and reduced prison terms by about 25-27 months. After Pulsifer, relief fell by 44 percentage points and prison terms rose by about 27 months. The Eleventh Circuit panel decision, its express vacatur, and the later en banc decision provide a separate within-circuit sequence. Sentence effects are smaller in a broader sample and larger where the drug minimum binds. Excluding zero-criminal-history defendants potentially affected by the 2023 Guidelines amendment leaves the reversal point estimate nearly unchanged but reduces its precision. Circuit-label permutation inference is also less precise, and the Lopez expansion window shows a sentence change outside the binding sample. In this setting, circuit precedent changed both statutory relief and time in prison.

detail.abstract: This study assesses the economic impact of the Japa phenomenon on Nigeria from 1981 to 2024. The research was conducted to evaluate how mass migration and the resulting brain drain affect national productivity and whether worker remittances provide a sufficient economic dividend to offset labor losses. Using an ex post-facto research design, the study utilizes a Vector Error Correction Model to analyze the long-run and short-run relationships between gross domestic product and key variables, including net migration, workers' remittances, foreign direct investment, and exchange rates. Empirical analysis reveals that net migration exerts a significant negative impact on Nigeria's economic performance, suggesting that the exodus of skilled professionals depletes the country's productive capacity. While home remittances contribute positively to the economy, their impact remains statistically inconclusive in the model. The findings also indicate that the intensity of this migration syndrome is driven by deteriorating domestic push factors such as unemployment and economic hardship coupled with increasingly attractive international pull factors. These results suggest that the Japa syndrome represents a critical structural challenge necessitating immediate and drastic policy intervention. The study highlights that relying on remittance inflows alone is insufficient to compensate for the loss of human capital. Consequently, these findings are vital for policymakers to prioritize strategies that accelerate domestic economic growth, enhance employability, and improve the business environment to retain talent. Strengthening these areas is essential to transition from a "run-for-your-life" migration mindset toward sustainable national development.

title: The Policing of Large-Scale Protests in Canada: Why Canada Needs a Public Order Police Act
affiliations: Thompson Rivers University - Faculty of Law

detail.title: The Policing of Large-Scale Protests in Canada: Why Canada Needs a Public Order Police Act

publicationDetails.detailsText: Robert Diab, “The Policing of Large-Scale Protests in Canada: Why Canada Needs a Public Order Policing Act” Report of the Public Inquiry into the 2022 Public Order Emergency, Volume 5: Policy Papers (February 2023)

detail.abstract:
Police lack clear authority in Canada to employ a common tactic to maintain order at large public events: the creation of exclusion zones around large portions of public space. Limited exceptions to this include powers in emergency law and a federal statute on intergovernmental conferences – powers that are unclear in scope. The common law does not authorize a large exclusion zone. Ontario’s resort to emergency powers in February of 2022 rendered Canada’s resort to an emergency redundant – as a tool to authorize the “secure area” in Ottawa used to bring the trucker convoy protest to an end.

The use of emergency law in 2022 was only the most recent in a series of attempts on the part of governments and courts in recent decades to address the gap in the law authorizing large exclusion zones in an ad hoc, temporary, and reactive fashion. Each case involved confusion among police, plans for the zone formulated in secret, and significant infringements of core rights and freedoms. Rights would be better protected and policing more effective by drawing on law from the UK and Australia. Lawmakers there have created comprehensive frameworks for policing large gatherings and events. Legislatures in Canada and its provinces should do the same and pass a bill dealing, respectively, with events of a national or provincial scope. A Public Order Police Act would provide a test for when police could erect a secure zone based on the principles of reasonable necessity and proportionality, and set out rules about admission, compensation, oversight, and review. This would be the most effective means of avoiding resort to emergency law and the cycle of confusion and disorder arising from temporary measures. It would also bring police conduct into closer conformity with the rule of law.

title: The Information-Responsibility Möbius Strip in the AI Era: A Theory of the Decision-Maker Paradox in Meso-Organizations
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: The Information-Responsibility Möbius Strip in the AI Era: A Theory of the Decision-Maker Paradox in Meso-Organizations
detail.abstract: This paper identifies a structural paradox in meso-organizations: when problems arise, implementers are let go before decision-makers. We argue that this pattern reflects an institutional coupling of the information layer and the responsibility layer-a coupling that forms what we name the Information-Responsibility Möbius Strip. In the pre-AI era, the coupling was latent because metrics were assumed neutral, and responsibility anchored on their scientific validity. AI removed this anchor-AI is ethically charged, responsibility cannot anchor on it, yet its use is mandated. This produced a closed loop: institution to information layer to responsibility layer to institution. Responsibility circulates infinitely, never anchoring. Decoupling-separating information from responsibility and re-anchoring responsibility to the subject that exercises judgment-resolves not only the layoff puzzle but also three broader problems: fairness and risk allocation, organizational contradictions, and selection systems. The paper contributes a new framework for understanding AI-era accountability and organizational design.

detail.abstract: This study reconstructs the historical transformation of selected settlements in Biliran, Philippines, through systematic analysis of secondary historical sources. Rather than producing another chronological history of the province, the study examines settlement persistence, relocation, renaming, administrative absorption, decline, and disappearance as processes of historical landscape transformation. The study draws on published historical accounts, local histories, historical timelines, scholarly literature, government records, and documented place-name evidence. A qualitative historical-documentary design was employed, using source criticism, cross-source comparison, chronological reconstruction, and settlement-trajectory analysis. The findings indicate that several contemporary settlements emerged through successive processes of renaming, territorial reorganization, administrative separation, incorporation, and relocation. Examples include the transformation of Gazebo into Naval, Bagongbong into Solano and subsequently Almeria, and Esperanza into Cabucgayan. Historical evidence also demonstrates that communities could retain spatial significance even when their original political or settlement identities changed. These patterns suggest that historical disappearance should not be interpreted simply as physical abandonment; it may also result from administrative restructuring, renaming, absorption, or selective historical remembrance. The study argues that reconstructing vanished and transformed settlements contributes to a more nuanced understanding of Biliran's historical geography and demonstrates how local historical landscapes are continuously reconstructed through documentary memory. The study contributes to Philippine historical geography by shifting attention from major political events toward the historical trajectories and mnemonic persistence of ordinary settlements.

title: Supply Chain Practice Bundles and Financial Resilience in Egyptian Manufacturing: A Synthetic Panel-Data Benchmark

detail.title: Supply Chain Practice Bundles and Financial Resilience in Egyptian Manufacturing: A Synthetic Panel-Data Benchmark

keywords: The Relationship Between Supply Chain Practice Bundles and Financial Resilience In Egyptian Manufacturing

detail.abstract: This completed study examines the relationship between supply chain practice bundles and financial resilience in Egyptian manufacturing through six-year synthetic firm panel, fixed-effects regression, and portfolio comparison. The analysis is anchored in a bounded fifteen-source Egyptian and MENA supply chain corpus and uses only those references. Across 540 firm-year observations, the fixed-effects coefficient of the practice bundle was 1.67 for ROA,-5.79 for cash-conversion days, and-7.84 for downside exposure. High-practice cases achieved mean ROA of 7.0% versus 4.9% in the low tier. The study contributes a reproducible analytical framework, explicit assumptions, numerical or coded results, tables, and code-generated figures. It does not claim that generated observations are measurements of Egyptian organizations. Its valid contribution is method validation, scenario comparison, decision sensitivity, or bounded content analysis. The paper concludes with managerial, policy, and research implications and specifies the evidence needed for external validation.

title: Manufacturing the Enemy: Definitional Instability, Political Instrumentalisation, and the Limits of Terrorism's Historiography

detail.title: Manufacturing the Enemy: Definitional Instability, Political Instrumentalisation, and the Limits of Terrorism's Historiography
detail.abstract: "The terrorist of yesterday is the hero of today, and the hero of yesterday becomes the terrorist of today." Eqbal Ahmad's observation captures a problem that terrorism studies has never resolved: there is no internationally agreed legal definition of terrorism, and the label is applied and withdrawn according to the interests of whoever controls it. This article argues that the distinction between terrorism and legitimate political violence is not merely contested but analytically indefensible as a stable category, and that this instability is not confined to policy and law; it runs through the discipline's own historiography. The influential debate between David Rapoport's "waves" model and Tom Parker and Nick Sitter's "strains" model, ostensibly a dispute about periodisation, is in fact a symptom of the same underlying problem Eqbal Ahmad identified: both frameworks attempt to impose a stable analytical order on a category that has never been stable, because it was never meant to be. The consequences of this instability are not academic. The same conceptual looseness that produces disagreement among historians is what allows states to detain without due process, freeze assets without judicial approval, invade without UN Security Council authorisation, and build surveillance architectures around targeted communities, all under the cover of a label that resists definition by design. AI Disclosure: Portions of this paper's editing were assisted by an AI language model (Anthropic's Claude). The research design, arguments, analysis, and conclusions are the author's own; the author reviewed and takes full responsibility for the final content.

title: Are Comprehensive Peace Agreements Overrated? Assessing the Case for Partial and Local Agreements as an Alternative Approach

detail.title: Are Comprehensive Peace Agreements Overrated? Assessing the Case for Partial and Local Agreements as an Alternative Approach
detail.abstract: Comprehensive peace agreements (CPAs) have long been treated as the benchmark instrument of post-Cold War conflict resolution, yet more than half fail within five years of signature. This paper argues that CPAs are overrated: not because comprehensiveness is a flawed goal, but because the label is routinely applied beyond its empirical scope, converting elite bargains that defer core grievances into what Bell and Pospisil term a "formalised political unsettlement" presented as final and durable. Drawing on cases including Oslo, the Juba Peace Agreement, Libya, Mozambique, Guatemala, Northern Ireland, Myanmar, Syria, and Sri Lanka, the paper weighs the structural case against CPAs against the genuine conditions under which they succeed, before assessing partial and local agreements as a fit-for-purpose, rather than wholesale, alternative. Partial agreements hold among signatories even when excluded parties continue fighting, and local agreements reach disputes national frameworks never touch, but both carry real limits and can be captured by the same elite interests they are meant to bypass. The paper closes by arguing that this entire debate presupposes a willingness to negotiate that a growing number of governments no longer have, as authoritarian conflict management increasingly substitutes control for compromise.

title: Last-100-Meter Vertical Delivery
affiliations: Beijing Institute of Technology, Beijing Institute of Technology, Tsinghua University and

detail.title: Last-100-Meter Vertical Delivery
detail.abstract: Problem Definition: On-demand delivery platforms increasingly distinguish themselves through faster and more reliable order fulfillment, yet the final delivery stage inside high-rise buildings can remain time-consuming and uncertain. We identify this overlooked stage as the last-100-meter vertical delivery problem and formalize it as the Elevator Delivery Problem with Deadlines (EDPD) under uncertain elevator waiting times. Elevator waiting-time data from Beijing office buildings show substantial dispersion, pronounced right tails, and systematic heterogeneity across call floors, requested travel directions, and elevator loading states. Methodology/results: To capture these empirical patterns, we use a directed network to distinguish elevator calls by call floor and requested travel direction and a scenario-wise ambiguity set to characterize each loading state with conditional moment and support information. To quantify delay risk, we propose the Flexible Essential Riskiness Index (FERI), which extends the Essential Riskiness Index (ERI) by allowing the ERI feasibility condition to be relaxed with a penalty. FERI jointly accounts for the probability and magnitude of lateness while remaining finite and informative in delay-prone instances, where ERI is inapplicable. Integrating these elements, we propose a last-100-meter vertical delivery model, derive an equivalent mixed-integer second-order cone reformulation, develop a Benders decomposition algorithm to solve the model exactly, and design a hybrid heuristic that combines a residual-capacity-based Label strategy with the Deadline and Floor strategies for real-time sequencing decisions. Managerial implications: Simulation experiments show that the Benders decomposition substantially improves tractability and that our proposed model provides more reliable out-of-sample performance than sample-average approximation under distributional misspecification. A case study using real elevator data from Weiya Building shows that the exact solution approach and the Label strategy outperform practical Floor and Deadline strategies. The results also show that reliable delivery sequences may accept additional but more predictable in-elevator riding time to avoid long and volatile waits. Mechanisms for platform--building coordination, including anticipatory elevator calling and dedicated elevator access, can further reduce vertical delivery delay risk. More broadly, this work highlights the role of vertical logistics in enabling reliable urban on-demand fulfillment.

title: From Organizational Immunity to Organizational Autoimmunity: Functional Reversal of Defensive Responses and Institutional Self-Harm
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: From Organizational Immunity to Organizational Autoimmunity: Functional Reversal of Defensive Responses and Institutional Self-Harm
detail.abstract:
This study theorizes how organizational defense can become a mechanism of organizational self-harm. Building on Hiraoka’s (2026a) Organizational Immune Model (OIM), which explains how internal disruption converges through Institutional Gap, Threat Redefinition, Procedural Reinforcement, Institutional Fixation, and Reintegration or Marginalization, this paper extends the model beyond defensive closure and introduces organizational autoimmunity.

Organizational autoimmunity is defined as a process in which mechanisms originally activated to protect organizational stability, order, legitimacy, or continuity misclassify internal self-corrective resources—such as problem-raising, expertise, dissent, documentation, and learning capacity—as threats and subsequently restrict or marginalize them. The defining feature of autoimmunity is therefore not excessive defensive intensity, but target misclassification. Loss of proportionality is treated as an amplification condition, while uncorrectability and institutional fixation are treated as conditions that stabilize and prolong self-harm.

The paper develops a nine-stage Organizational Autoimmune Escalation Model linking internal problem-raising, threat recognition, interpersonal avoidance, managerial vacancy, procedural substitution, narrative and role inversion, institutional self-binding, defensive evidence generation, and externalization. These processes may produce four forms of organizational self-harm: human self-harm, cognitive self-harm, institutional self-harm, and self-harm to legitimacy and legal stability. Post-Conflict Repair Capacity (PCRC), defined as the capacity to restore ordinary interaction after conflict without fixing the other party as a permanent threat, is proposed as a buffering mechanism.

The framework also explains how locally rational and non-malicious actions can aggregate into organization-level behavior that appears persistently hostile. Organizational autoimmunity therefore shifts attention from whether defense restores short-term order to what capacities the organization loses while defending itself.

title: National Determinants of Coffee Prices in Italy: an Econometric Analysis

detail.title: National Determinants of Coffee Prices in Italy: an Econometric Analysis

detail.abstract: Coffee is one of the most widespread and culturally significant consumer goods in Italy: the domestic market is currently worth around €5.2 billion, with per capita consumption of approximately 5.5 kg per year. This paper analyses the determinants of coffee consumer prices in Italy over the period 2013-2025, using a monthly dataset constructed by integrating Eurostat, ECB, World Bank and national sources. The estimated multiple OLS regression model includes both national variables energy costs, general inflation, interest rates and labour costs and international variables oil prices and the euro/dollar exchange rate with the discussion of results focused on national determinants. Complementing the analysis with a multicollinearity test (VIF), an endogeneity test using instrumental variables, and the Hausman test, the study shows that electricity prices and the interest rate are the most robust determinants of coffee prices in Italy. The analysis is completed by an ARIMA-GARCH model of the Italian coffee price time series, which reveals a significant seasonal structure and high volatility persistence (α+β ≈ 0.95). The results provide useful insights for understanding the domestic transmission of inflationary pressures on coffee prices and for assessing the adaptation strategies of households and the national supply chain.

title: Between Stars and Shadows: The Survival Saga of Deep Tech Dreamers
affiliations: , University of Campinas, EDHEC Business School,  and Indian Institute of Technology Bombay

detail.title: Between Stars and Shadows: The Survival Saga of Deep Tech Dreamers
detail.abstract: Deep tech startups, built on advanced scientific and engineering innovations, play a crucial role in driving technological progress across sectors such as artificial intelligence, biotechnology, and quantum computing. However, their survival is challenged by long development cycles, complex regulatory environments, capital intensity, and market resistance. This study explores the survival dynamics of deep tech startups through a systematic review and bibliometric analysis of scholarly literature from the last 50 years, integrating theories such as the resourcebased view, dynamic capabilities, organizational ecology, and institutional theory. Key survival determinants include technological innovation, human capital, funding mechanisms, strategic partnerships, and policy alignment. The findings reveal that survival extends beyond financial stability to include ecosystem integration, resilience against market disruptions, and technological leadership. The bibliometric analysis highlights emerging research clusters, global collaboration patterns, and evolving thematic priorities. A proposed research agenda emphasizes interdisciplinary approaches, including the integration of technological innovation with social and economic frameworks, regulatory reforms tailored to streamline compliance in high tech industries, sustainable funding models such as hybrid mechanisms combining venture capital and public grants, and adaptive market strategies that prioritize customer education, strategic partnerships, and regional ecosystem development. This study offers theoretical contributions and actionable insights for entrepreneurs, investors, policymakers, and academic researchers dedicated to fostering a resilient deep tech innovation ecosystem.

title: Hybrid Warfare Perception: Evidence from Europe

detail.title: Hybrid Warfare Perception: Evidence from Europe
detail.abstract: Since the war in Ukraine began, Europe has been increasingly facing hybrid attacks on critical infrastructure, drone flights over sensitive military sites, or disinformation campaigns. In this paper, I estimate panel local projections to study how the hybrid warfare perception influences financial markets. I construct a novel news-based Hybrid Warfare Perception Index for Europe to investigate how financial markets respond to hybrid warfare. Using a panel setting based on major european countries, I find that more intense hybrid warfare perception raises geopolitical and credit risk, while consumer and business sentiment deteriorate, similarly to a classic uncertainty shock. Moreover, I find evidence of a steepening of the term spread, which possibly reflect how investors adjust their expectations about risk on longer durations. I also investigate country-specific effects of hybrid warfare perception, from which I can confirm heterogeneous effects across countries.

detail.abstract: This article provides a critical and analytical examination of the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (NTA). This landmark legislative reform repeals and consolidates over ten major tax statutes, including the Companies Income Tax Act (CITA) and the Personal Income Tax Act (PITA) in order to create a unified fiscal framework for Nigeria. Rather than offering just a summary of the Act, this article makes a significant attempt to evaluate its policy direction, practical implications, and theoretical consistency, relying on a doctrinal methodology. To ensure an uninterrupted flow, the article provides a clarification of key terms such as "company," "tax," and "resident person," as these concepts form the foundational basis for tax liability and privileges. It further delves into the most transformative provisions introduced by the NTA, including the 0% tax rate for small companies, the ₦800,000 personal income tax exemption threshold, the taxation of digital and virtual assets under section 4(1)(j), and the standardised 4% development levy. Every analysis provided is supported by verifiable statutory citations from the NTA 2025 and the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025 (NTAA). The article concludes with bespoke recommendations for a clearer implementation process, particularly regarding ambiguous thresholds and the burden of proof for exemptions, to ensure the new law aligns with the objectives of equity and administrative efficiency throughout Nigeria.

detail.abstract: Countries outside the artificial-intelligence frontier face a difficult choice because reproducing frontier models may exceed their financial and organizational capacity, while buying access through closed interfaces leaves limited control over the underlying technology. This article examines an intermediate route based on the repeated and lawful adaptation of externally developed open-weight models to local conditions and calls the associated mechanism learning through cumulative adaptation. Extending the distinction between learning by doing and learning by using, the concept locates learning in adaptation episodes whose methods, outcomes, and diagnoses are retained in ways that inform later decisions. The qualifier cumulative refers to reusable institutional competence rather than uninterrupted performance improvement, while know-to denotes the task-level ability to obtain a desired result from a system without fully understanding its internal mechanisms and is distinguished from technical know-how and organizational control capability. Brazilian evidence gives empirical content to the proposed account of tropicalization with local competence. Sabiá documents adaptation and evaluation, the Plano Brasileiro de Inteligência Artificial (PBIA) specifies planned enabling conditions, and Rio 3.5 records public-sector entry into model-level operations within a municipal technology company. Across these institutional levels, the cases provide complementary evidence of the technical, policy, and organizational preconditions for a credible intermediate route toward catch-up. A contextual comparison with national and supranational strategies situates the Brazilian configuration within a wider range of capability-building pathways and shows how technological autonomy may be developed selectively across layers.

title:
The Last Price
Model Identity and Consumer Welfare in Agentic Bargaining

detail.title:
The Last Price
Model Identity and Consumer Welfare in Agentic Bargaining
detail.abstract: As autonomous language-model agents begin to search, negotiate, and transact on behalf of consumers, the computational system representing a buyer may itself become an economically consequential input. This paper tests that possibility in a bilateral bargaining experiment whose protocol, executable action space, primary outcomes, and analysis were pre-specified and version-control frozen before execution. I construct economically identical buyer environments and vary only the language model acting as the buyer, holding fixed the seller model, product, buyer value, budget, seller cost, information regime, move order, bargaining protocol, and feasible action space. Three open-weight buyer models-Qwen 3 1.7B, Gemma 3 4B, and Llama 3.2 3B-are evaluated across 216 matched bargaining environments. The experiment contains 702 episodes: 648 bargaining episodes and 54 posted-price controls. The complete technical gate passes with no missing cells, infrastructure failures, invalid finite-menu choices, budget violations, cost violations, or incomplete matched blocks. Agreement occurs in 56.48% of Llama episodes, compared with 18.06% for Qwen and 15.28% for Gemma. A matched Cochran Q test rejects equality across models (Q = 118.768; Holm-adjusted p = 1.62 × 10^-26). Mean unconditional normalized realized buyer surplus is 0.1340 for Llama, 0.0125 for Qwen, and 0 for Gemma; a Friedman test likewise rejects equality (chi-square = 192.147; Holm-adjusted p = 3.78 × 10^-42). The narrow conclusion is that, within this controlled agentic market, changing the model representing an otherwise identical buyer changes both trade formation and realized buyer welfare. Because all buyers face one fixed Qwen 3 4B seller policy, the estimated representation effects are local to that strategic counterparty. The design does not identify model capability itself as the causal mechanism and does not imply a universal ranking of models.

title: Connected to the Committee: FOMC Networks and Firm Exposure to Monetary Policy

detail.title: Connected to the Committee: FOMC Networks and Firm Exposure to Monetary Policy
detail.abstract: Do private ties to monetary policymakers matter? We map business links between FOMC members and public firms from 1970 to 2024. Connected firms earn about 2 percent when their contacts enter Federal Reserve leadership and about 70 basis points more than comparable firms after top-quintile hawkish FOMC surprises. The premium appears during FOMC service and is absent for inactive ties. In matched FR Y-9C data, connected public bank holding companies raise liabilities, reduce cash, and expand loans before the most hawkish surprises. Monetary-policy exposure also reflects professional networks around policymakers.

title: Ground-Truthing Latency Alpha: An Independent Test of LLM-Semantic-Extraction Alpha in EIA-Driven Crude Oil Futures

detail.title: Ground-Truthing Latency Alpha: An Independent Test of LLM-Semantic-Extraction Alpha in EIA-Driven Crude Oil Futures

declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Pape (2025) reports that real-time LLM-based semantic extraction of the EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report yields a tradeable, low-latency signal in crude oil futures (Sharpe ~1.82). We test this thesis independently on a retail capital-efficient stack by decomposing it into two falsifiable sub-claims: (A) a measurable post-release alpha that decays rapidly (the "latency" claim), and (B) that a multi-field / semantic read of the whole report outperforms a single-crude-inventory-surprise number (the "semantic richness" claim). Our method is staged by cost, where a zero-cost parallel observer captures the second-to-minute reaction at each live release; a near-zero-cost historical tick data study measures the sub-second-to-second reaction and its half-life; and an optional low-latency live test estimates the achievable retail capture. The first results (Tier 1, n=10 real EIA releases, CME CL front-month trades) directly test claim (A); the instantaneous release jump captures, on average, only 3.5% of the eventual 30-minute move; the first 30 seconds are net noise (a slight fade), and approximately 40% of the move is realized only by the five-minute mark. Thus, there is no meaningful sub-second repricing to trade crude in this event. A matched placebo control run at scale (149 EIA vs. 146 non-EIA windows over three years) then separates the two questions. In our retail setting, the latency mechanism does not transfer; the instantaneous jump is negligible, and the entry latency across the sub-second-to-30-second range is immaterial. However, the slower minute-scale is genuinely EIA-specific: EIA windows move crude about 1.30x the matched non-EIA windows (Mann-Whitney p = 0.0075), a real if small volatility premium that a smaller ten-release sample had missed as non-significant (p = 0.256), affirming our premise that the release moves the market. We then test whether the premium is directionally harvested. A proxy-consensus screen gives only a faint, non-significant hint (single-crude 57.4%, p = 0.084), and a direct implementation of the semantic method using a language model reading the full multi-field report and issuing a directional call, scored blind over 149 releases does no better (54.1%, p = 0.37) and does not out-predict the single-crude number. We conclude that, for a retail, non-co-located crude/EIA implementation, a tradeable directional edge is not recoverable above chance, most plausibly because the released figures are largely anticipated, which bounds the retail-reachable version and is offered as a complement to, not a contradiction of, the results obtained with institutional infrastructure.

title: Sixty-Four Words of Guidance: Disclosure Design and Narrative Credibility Within Form 8-K
affiliations: , Auburn University - Department of Finance and The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

detail.title: Sixty-Four Words of Guidance: Disclosure Design and Narrative Credibility Within Form 8-K
detail.abstract: Mandatory disclosure rules differ sharply in codification. We study how such disclosure settings may fall short by exploiting within-form variation in Form 8-K: while most items are tightly specified, the residual “Other Events” item is governed by only 64 words. We document OE disclosures receive substantially less regulatory scrutiny: their odds of receiving an SEC comment letter are 70.5% lower, and such scrutiny does not respond detectably to red flags, unlike its codified counterparts. Optimistic tone in this weakly codified channel predicts stronger announcement returns, subsequent reversals, and weaker future operating performance; tone in non-OE predicts drift and stronger fundamentals. Holding the OE setting fixed, enforcement exposure and regulatory intensity attenuate these patterns. The effects are strongest for hard-to-verify, nonfinancial topics, frequently appear before corporate events where short-lived price pressure may benefit managers or firms, and intensify with retail-oriented attention and trading. Overall, codification and scrutiny, rather than mandatory status alone, are associated with the credibility of strategic narrative disclosure.

title: The Wisdom of Crowds: Information Aggregation with Online Ratings
affiliations: Shiv Nadar University and Ashoka University

detail.title: The Wisdom of Crowds: Information Aggregation with Online Ratings
detail.abstract: We develop a social learning framework to study the aggregation properties of online ratings. The self-reported nature of ratings leads to only extreme reviews being posted. Thus, the history can not distinguish between a past agent who purchases but does not leave a rating, and an agent who does not purchase. This reduces the informational content of the reviews. Even under unbounded private signal, we show that learning can be incomplete: belief converges to an intermediate value. Under bounded belief, however, ratings improve the social learning.

title: From Esg Attributes to Resilience Capabilities
affiliations: Nyenrode Business University

detail.title: From Esg Attributes to Resilience Capabilities

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I want to thank Professor Willem Schramada at Nyenrode Business University for his advice and guidance as my supervisor.

detail.abstract: Attribute-based ESG assessment tells investors what a company has disclosed or adopted. It does not tell them what the company can do under pressure. I argue that long-term institutional investors should shift their primary unit of sustainability assessment from attributes to capabilities. The shift extends rather than discards existing practice: leading ESG analysis is already moving towards forward-looking transition-credibility assessment, which the framework developed here systematises. Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory, resilience ecology and empirical resilience research, the framework applies three capability dimensions (sensing, seizing and reconfiguring) across three investment time horizons and five connected investment activities, preceded by a mandate conversation that settles the investor's objectives. A second axis disciplines the assessment: capability evidence must show not only that a firm's adaptive capacity is improving, but that its adaptation reduces rather than transfers systemic risk. Whether and on what ground a spillover enters the investment judgement depends on the investor's mandate and, where financial transmission is claimed, on how broadly the portfolio is diversified. The framework is an instrument for better longterm investment judgement, not a mechanism for delivering real-economy outcomes. I set out a minimum viable assessment that analysts can apply today, state the framework's limitations, and define the validation agenda that follows. I also consider artificial intelligence as an emerging means of scaling capability evidence across large portfolios, supporting rather than replacing analyst judgement.

title: Rogers Revisited — Applying Diffusion of Innovations Theory to Solar PV, Electric Vehicles, and AI Adoption Curves in Developing Economies

detail.title: Rogers Revisited — Applying Diffusion of Innovations Theory to Solar PV, Electric Vehicles, and AI Adoption Curves in Developing Economies
detail.abstract: This paper re‑examines Diffusion of Innovations theory within the context of developing economies, arguing that classical Rogersian models—built around stable institutions, predictable communication channels, and high social trust—do not fully capture the dynamics present in low‑income or rapidly transforming environments. The study synthesizes empirical findings from recent development research to show how informal networks, state capacity constraints, market frictions, and nonlinear adoption incentives reshape diffusion pathways. It proposes an updated framework emphasizing institutional volatility, resource scarcity, and collective‑risk decision‑making, demonstrating that innovation adoption in developing economies often follows punctuated, cluster‑driven patterns rather than smooth S‑curves. The paper concludes by outlining policy implications for governments, NGOs, and private‑sector actors seeking to accelerate technology uptake under conditions of structural fragility.

title: Strategic Liquidity Absorption as Information Elicitation in Hidden Microstructure Equilibria
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Strategic Liquidity Absorption as Information Elicitation in Hidden Microstructure Equilibria
detail.abstract: This paper studies a strategic liquidity entrant that changes the informativeness of observed order flow by reducing the variance of non-informative flow. The central object is not price volatility itself, but the conditional variance of the residual order-flow component that provides camouflage to informed trading. We build the mechanism from a static Bayesian market-making problem, derive the incumbent's equilibrium trading intensity from first principles, and show that, with strictly positive execution frictions, statistical precision about the informed component rises as residual noise variance falls, even though the informed trader optimally reduces its trading intensity. The paper then embeds this result in a two-incumbent "stalemate" environment with approximately offsetting positions. The key identification boundary is explicit: exact cancellation in an aggregate tape makes an incumbent-specific stress state unidentifiable unless that state changes an observable statistic. A forced-liquidation stage is therefore modeled only as a conditional continuation game, not as an automatic consequence of volatility suppression. Finally, a K-entrant extension shows how non-rival information creates a free-rider problem and under-provision of aggregate absorption relative to a symmetric social optimum. The resulting framework is a mechanism hypothesis with testable predictions, rather than a claim that liquidity suppression mechanically forces liquidation in real markets.

detail.title: Climate Risk and Homeowners Insurance Non-Renewals: Real Effects on Foreclosures and Local Economies
detail.abstract: Research shows that increased homeowners insurance premiums strain household finances and that home foreclosures depress local economic activity. Motivated by the growing uninsurability of homes in climate-risky areas, we examine effects of insurer-initiated nonrenewals of homeowners insurance policies using county-year non-renewals during 2018-2023 from the U.S. Senate Budget Committee. We expect that non-renewals have more economically and socially adverse effects than premium increases because non-renewals suggest insurers cannot adequately evaluate, manage, or price risks, and because mortgage contracts require hazard insurance on the mortgaged property. We first show that non-renewals are positively associated with three-year average climate-disaster damages in that county and in other counties in the state, with these associations concentrated in states that are served by financially weaker insurers, that require pre-approval of insurance rates, and that experience more uncertain climate-disaster losses. We then estimate the effects of non-renewals on foreclosures and local economic variables using a shift-share-style instrument for non-renewals and find that instrumented non-renewals are significantly positively associated with foreclosure rates, with this association concentrated in states with fewer insurers, no insurer of last resort, and non-judicial foreclosure. We further find that these effects of non-renewals are concentrated in counties with more socially vulnerable populations. Lastly, we find that instrumented non-renewals are associated with reduced housing values (especially for low-value properties), retail sales, and homeownership rates, with most of these effects being larger in high-foreclosure counties. Our findings suggest that preserving housing insurability given accelerating climate change is a central challenge for policymakers.

title: The Habenular Vice Shame Without a Witness
